security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, Java examples, placeholder Azure configuration, and reference links. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or executable installer code was found in SKILL.md. Users should still keep real Application Insights connection strings out of prompts and documentation.

remediation.issue: Connection string examples can be mistaken for a place to paste production secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear note that real Application Insights connection strings should be stored in environment variables or a secret manager.

remediation.issue: The documented exporter package is deprecated.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the migration warning prominent and direct new projects to azure-monitor-opentelemetry-autoconfigure.

content.user_title: Configure Azure Monitor Telemetry for Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable telemetry setup without sorting through deprecated exporter guidance. This skill explains Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry patterns and migration steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains the deprecated exporter dependency and the recommended autoconfigure replacement.
Shows Application Insights connection string configuration with an environment variable placeholder.
Provides Java examples for creating spans, nesting spans, and recording exceptions.
Describes span attributes, custom span processors, and OpenTelemetry metrics.
Links to Azure SDK, Maven Central, OpenTelemetry, and Application Insights references.
limitations: It does not install packages or run Maven commands by itself.
It uses placeholder versions and connection strings; users must verify current Azure SDK versions.
It focuses on Java and does not cover .NET, Python, or JavaScript exporters.
It describes a deprecated exporter, so new projects should prefer autoconfigure guidance.

use_cases.title: Migrate Legacy Java Telemetry
use_cases.description: Plan replacement of the deprecated Azure Monitor exporter with the autoconfigure package.

use_cases.title: Add Distributed Tracing
use_cases.description: Instrument Java services with spans, attributes, exception recording, and parent-child trace structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Guidance
use_cases.description: Create team guidance for Azure Monitor traces, metrics, and Application Insights setup.

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this Java service should send traces and metrics to Azure Monitor. Keep the answer focused on current recommended packages.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Java telemetry plan and outline the steps to move from azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter to autoconfigure.

prompt_templates.title: Review Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my proposed span names, attributes, exception handling, and metrics for a Java service using Azure Monitor.

prompt_templates.title: Design Observability Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise observability standard for Java teams using OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor, and Application Insights.

output_examples.input: A team asks whether to use the deprecated exporter in a new Java service.
output_examples.output: The response recommends autoconfigure, explains why the exporter is deprecated, and lists migration checks before implementation.

output_examples.input: A developer needs better trace detail for order processing.
output_examples.output: The response suggests clear span names, stable attributes, exception recording, and parent-child span structure for the workflow.

output_examples.input: An SRE wants metrics guidance for request count and latency.
output_examples.output: The response describes counters, histograms, semantic attributes, and dashboards that separate traffic volume from request duration.

best_practices: Prefer the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry autoconfigure package for new Java projects.
Store real Application Insights connection strings in environment variables or a secret manager.
Use meaningful span names, semantic attributes, and finally blocks that always end spans.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production instrumentation keys or connection strings into prompts.
Do not build new services around the deprecated exporter unless a legacy constraint requires it.
Do not record sensitive customer data in span names, attributes, logs, or exception messages.

faq.question: Is this skill for new Java projects?
faq.answer: It can help, but new projects should use Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry autoconfigure instead of the deprecated exporter.

faq.question: Can it configure Application Insights connection strings?
faq.answer: It explains the expected configuration pattern, but users should manage real values through secure environment or secret systems.

faq.question: Does it cover metrics as well as traces?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OpenTelemetry examples for request counters and latency histograms.

faq.question: Does it run code or install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides documentation guidance and examples only.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should teams verify before using the examples?
faq.answer: Teams should verify current Azure SDK versions, package status, data privacy rules, and their Application Insights resource settings.
